descriptions.title: Vendor-neutral by construction (no hardcoded model names)
descriptions.body: The whole AI layer is data-driven. settings.json declares a list of vendors, each with a module + class name; VendorRegistry uses importlib to load only the active ones, and VendorRouter resolves a request to a concrete vendor by prefer → configured default → first active-with-capability → RuntimeError. Adding a model means editing JSON, not code. ClaudeVendor is the only adapter active by default; OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp are pre-wired and off until a key or endpoint is supplied. This is a deliberate anti-lock-in stance: an institution can run entirely on local models (Ollama/LM Studio/llama.cpp) with zero cloud calls and zero data egress.

descriptions.title: Why fixture mode is the default today (and why status is pre-POC)
descriptions.body: CogniBase has never connected to a live OnBase deployment. OnBaseSource runs in mode=auto, which tries the REST client and falls back to local fixtures the moment it fails — and it always fails, because OnBaseRestClient is an unexercised stub and UnityClient raises NotImplementedError. So every doc-type, lifecycle, and extract you see is read from parsed .expk exports, a sample schema.json, and *WorkflowDoc*.json, with synthetic populated counts. The code paths are real and tested; the data is not live. That gap — fixtures vs a real OnBase connection (M2/M3) — is exactly why the registry status is pre_poc rather than poc.

descriptions.title: The capability safety boundary (sqlglot validator)
descriptions.body: Admin-Authored Capabilities let a human write SQL that end-users later run, so the SQL is the attack surface. capabilities/validator.py parses it with sqlglot (sqlite dialect) and rejects anything that isn't a single read-only SELECT: multi-statements, any Insert/Update/Delete/Drop/Alter/Create/Pragma/Attach/Merge node anywhere in the tree, sqlite_/pragma_ identifiers, table-valued functions, tables outside the capability's declared anchors, and :placeholders not declared as parameters. It runs at publish time AND again at run time (defense in depth — the JSON could be hand-edited between the two). This is what makes user-authored SQL safe enough to expose.

descriptions.title: Files as the source of truth — no database, no migrations
descriptions.body: Anchors, workspaces, bridges, and capabilities are each persisted as one JSON file under Product/Lake. The file IS the record: UI editing, agent generation, hand-editing, and git all hit the same artifact, and there is no schema-migration burden. Capability edits write a CapabilityVersion snapshot so history is preserved. The only 'database' anywhere is the per-run, in-memory SQLite the LakeBackend builds from anchor JSONL and then throws away — there is no persistent relational store to corrupt or back up.

descriptions.title: Anchors + the Lake backend: scoped, sandboxed execution
descriptions.body: An Anchor declares a slice of a source (a doc type, keyword set, or lifecycle). Materializing it writes raw JSONL to Product/Lake/raw/<source>/<anchor>/ and optionally embeds the records into a dedicated Chroma collection anchor_<id>. When a capability runs, LakeBackend loads ONLY the anchors that capability declared into an in-memory SQLite database (one TEXT table per anchor) and executes the validated SQL there. The anchor list is therefore enforced twice: by the validator (no out-of-anchor tables) and by the backend (only declared anchors are even loaded).

descriptions.title: Provenance and audit on every run
descriptions.body: Two provenance layers run end to end. Every extracted record carries a _provenance block (source, source_id, retrieved_at, method, confidence) stamped by AbstractSource.annotate(). Every capability run — preview or real — calls generate_audit_summary(), which writes a .docx plus a .json sidecar pinning the capability version, the bound parameters, the backend snapshot id, and the returned rows. Because the version is pinned at run time, the audit reproduces byte-for-byte even after the capability is later edited. This is the feature that differentiates CogniBase from a generic BI tool: the answer ships with its own receipt.
